bullet_feedback.bullet: Because the 270K+ row PostgreSQL workflow table had strict access limits, precomputed popular workflows into a category tree that the Claude skill searches first, with Redis caching full workflows to cut database queries
bullet_feedback.problem: Opens with the constraint ('Because the 270K+ row PostgreSQL workflow table had strict access limits') before saying what was built, and 'the Claude skill' is introduced as if the reader already knows what it is. The bullet ends at 'to cut database queries', which is a mechanism, not something a user or team gained.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: I could not restate this to a hiring manager without guessing what the 'Claude skill' is or who benefited. On a skim it reads as a string of tech nouns (PostgreSQL, category tree, Claude skill, Redis) and gets skipped.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the 'Claude skill' is (the AI assistant that generates workflows from the previous bullet?) and what the category tree let it do that it couldn't before
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the verb and the thing built, name the AI assistant in plain words once, then give the constraint as the reason. Consider merging with the 65% bullet so the AI feature is introduced once, e.g. 'Built a category index of popular workflows for the AI workflow generator to search first, because direct access to the 270K-row workflow table was restricted, and cached full workflows in Redis'.

bullet_feedback.bullet: For a PhD-led robotics project targeting ICLR, built a Python pipeline that draws AnyGrasp candidates from multi-camera images as Open3D overlays and tuned prompts so a vision-language model picks the right grasp more often
bullet_feedback.problem: 'AnyGrasp candidates', 'Open3D overlays' and 'ICLR' are three insider terms in one sentence, and the goal (helping a robot choose how to grab an object) is never said in plain words. 'picks the right grasp more often' has no indication of how much more often or how it was checked.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A recruiter can't tell what was built or why it mattered, so the bullet reads as filler under a research-intern title and adds nothing to the screen.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: in plain words, what the robot is trying to do and what the pipeline's output is; whether 'more often' was measured
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: State the task first ('help a robot choose where to grab an object'), then the method, and keep only the one tool name that explains the engineering. 'targeting ICLR' could become 'research project (ICLR submission)' or be cut.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Compared B+ tree and LSM skip-list storage for the engine's event logs on identical 2M-record workloads: the B+ tree read 12.8x faster and answered range queries 22x faster, at the cost of 27% more disk
bullet_feedback.problem: The bullet reports a benchmark but not the decision it led to or why storage choice matters for an order book. 'B+ tree' and 'LSM skip-list' mean nothing to a non-engineer, so the 12.8x and 22x numbers float with no meaning.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This reads like a homework comparison rather than an engineering decision; a recruiter skips it, and a hiring manager wonders whether anything was chosen as a result.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: which storage the engine ended up using and why that tradeoff fit the engine's workload
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Frame it as a choice: 'Chose X for the engine's event log after benchmarking it against Y on 2M records: ...'. Keep one speed number rather than two to reduce density.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Automated retraining for a production Amazon Bedrock model that sorts research documents by importance: on an EventBridge schedule a larger LLM grades it, and it is fine-tuned only when those grades shift past a threshold
bullet_feedback.problem: 'a larger LLM grades it' is ambiguous: 'it' could mean the model or the documents. The second half switches to passive voice ('it is fine-tuned'), so it is unclear what the candidate built versus what happens automatically.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The idea (only retrain when quality drifts) is strong but takes two readings to get, and a recruiter loses the ownership signal.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the larger LLM grades (the model's rankings?)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Make the candidate the subject throughout and name what gets graded, e.g. '...set up a scheduled check where a larger LLM grades the model's rankings, and retraining runs only when those grades drift past a threshold'. 'EventBridge' can live in Skills.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Deployed a space-topic research tool for Amazon Leo's public-policy team and set it up for handoff with AWS CDK infrastructure-as-code and GitHub Actions CI/CD, so Leo engineers new to the project now maintain it on AWS Fargate
bullet_feedback.problem: 'space-topic research tool' doesn't say what the tool does for the policy team, and 'Amazon Leo' is not a name every recruiter knows. Three tool names (AWS CDK, GitHub Actions, Fargate) sit in the middle of the sentence.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The handoff outcome (Amazon engineers now maintain it) is a strong signal but is buried after the tool list.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the tool does for the public-policy team in a few plain words
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Say what the tool does before the tech, and move one or two tool names to Skills so the handoff outcome is reached sooner.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Building a RAG meal-suggestion feature for the official UMD app (GPT-4o mini, ChromaDB + SentenceBERT search); 93% of generated meals rated satisfactory by internal testers
bullet_feedback.problem: The parenthetical '(GPT-4o mini, ChromaDB + SentenceBERT search)' and the semicolon make this read as a stitched note rather than a sentence; 'RAG' is unexplained.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Minor human-voice cost; it is the one bullet that reads like a tech dump.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Turn the parenthetical into a short clause that says what the search does (e.g. finds similar meals before the model writes a suggestion) and replace the semicolon with a connecting phrase.

page_feedback.problem: The strongest systems evidence (the IEX order book: 50.9M messages, 1.26M events/sec) sits at the bottom under Projects, while the top half is dominated by AI-assistant and AWS-service work.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: The intended profile is 'systems-oriented engineer'; on a 10-second skim I came away with 'AWS and AI apps' and only noticed the systems project because of the bold numbers. A reviewer who stops at Experience misses the best technical story.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Consider whether the order-book project can be surfaced higher (e.g. Projects above some Experience entries is unusual, so alternatively trim UMIACS/TerpLabs bullets so Projects lands higher on the page).

page_feedback.problem: Five experience entries with three marked 'Present' plus a project make the page dense; UMIACS and the second TerpLabs bullet were the parts I skipped entirely.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Each extra entry dilutes attention from the brand names and headline wins that carry the screen.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Cut or compress the weakest bullet (UMIACS robotics or TerpLabs meal feature) rather than adding anything.

page_feedback.problem: Nine bolded numbers across the page (90%, 65%, 34%, 30%, 20,000+, 93%, 50.9M, 12.8x, 1.26M); on a skim the eye jumps between them without the context of what each measures.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: Bold works as an anchor only when sparse; the less important ones (30%, 93%, 12.8x) compete with the headline ones.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep bold on the 3-4 numbers that tell the main story and unbold the rest.

page_feedback.problem: Several role names need outside knowledge: 'Amazon Leo' and 'UMIACS' are not self-explanatory to a recruiter.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: A confused skim slows the reader at the exact point where brand recognition should be helping.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Let the first bullet under each say in plain words what the organization or team does, without adding new facts.
